# Program review: the 2026-08 campaign {#sec-program-review-2026-08}

::: {.callout-note title="What this chapter is"}
This chapter is the authoritative synthesis of the research program as of
2026-09-03. It supersedes the earlier "future directions" chapter (whose open
questions have all since been measured) and compresses roughly ninety
preregistered training runs, four adversarial probes, and three architecture
generations into the tables and verdicts a reviewer actually needs. The
frontier table is computed live from the committed reduction artifacts in
`results/`, and every claim links to the dated lab-notebook entry
(@sec-notebook) where it was preregistered and read out. The campaign
narrative (@sec-review-arc) ends 2026-08-19; the refutation wave that
followed (@sec-review-refutation-wave) resolved every mechanism candidate
then open. An independent critic review on 2026-09-02
(`results/critic_review_2026-09-02.md`, recorded at @sec-nb-critic-review)
then found that several of this chapter's claims were contradicted by the
program's own code and artifacts; @sec-review-reframing records what was
retired, what replaced it, and the evidence for each. Read that section
before quoting anything from the earlier ones. The live tech-tree ledger is
@sec-tech-tree.
:::

## The one-paragraph verdict

The program set out to build a boundary-driven-PDE surrogate whose
generalization comes from **declared physical structure** rather than data
coverage. After a falsification campaign against the strongest available baseline (GeoTransolver, a soft-slice global-attention architecture), the
result is a *decomposition*: *accuracy* at industrial scale comes
from normalized global routing and rich features, and GeoTransolver had it;
*pose robustness* is a contract MT2 holds by construction and GeoTransolver
recovers by canonicalization at 1.01$\times$ cost whenever a freestream
direction and a resolvable principal frame exist — which is every vehicle
dataset in this program (@sec-nb-p1pp-verdict); *cross-family transfer*
comes from training-data diversity, not from any architecture we tested;
and *query-independence* — the ability to evaluate the surrogate anywhere
without the answer depending on which other points are sampled — trades
directly against accuracy in every design we built. The program's product
is `MeshTransformer2` (MT2): GeoTransolver's routing on SE(3)-invariant
features, with exact rotation/translation covariance paid once at the
network's edges. Honestly stated (@sec-review-reframing), MT2 is at
in-family parity with GeoTransolver on HiLiftAeroML (MT2/GT = 0.98 at each
architecture's best learning rate) and 1.085$\times$ behind on DrivAerML at
best-vs-best rates; it trains stably across a learning-rate decade where
GeoTransolver degrades 4--14$\times$; with the similarity gauge it is the
most density-robust architecture measured (1.20$\times$ under 10:1 sampling
bias versus GeoTransolver's 3.6$\times$); and it costs about twice
GeoTransolver's peak training memory (9.8 GB vs 4.6 GB) on the same
protocol.

## The result that matters: data efficiency on HiLiftAeroML {#sec-review-data-efficiency}

Everything else in this chapter is a fair-comparison ledger; this is the
one measurement where the two architectures separate by more than a
seed spread on a production dataset. On HiLiftAeroML's curated
data-efficiency splits — 35, 210 and 1,260 training cases, all scored on
the *same* 180-case validation set — MeshTransformer2 (MT2) is 2.9x more
accurate than GeoTransolver at 35 cases and 2.5x at 210, converging to
parity at 1,260 (@fig-hilift-data-efficiency). The seed spreads are an
order of magnitude smaller than the gaps. Put differently: MT2 trained on
210 cases reaches the accuracy GeoTransolver needs 1,260 cases to reach.
This is the axis the program's north-star correction named first, and the
first architecture-driven generalization advantage the program has
measured in 3D (@sec-nb-hl-ladder-dataeff).

```{python}
#| label: fig-hilift-data-efficiency
#| fig-cap: >
#|   Data efficiency on HiLiftAeroML. Pressure relative L2 error on the
#|   shared 180-case validation set versus number of training cases, for
#|   GeoTransolver (red circles) and MeshTransformer2 (blue squares); lines
#|   join seed means, shaded bands span the two seeds, small dots are the
#|   individual seeds; the annotated factor is GeoTransolver's error divided
#|   by MT2's at the same rung. Assumptions held fixed for both architectures:
#|   learning rate 1e-3 (each architecture's best on the full split, chosen
#|   by validation before the ladder ran), 500 epochs, bfloat16, no
#|   augmentation, 10,000 sampled surface points per case, two seeds. MT2
#|   is the v3c constant-gauge configuration (these lanes predate the
#|   similarity gauge). The test split is sealed and untouched.
#|   Provisional until the preregistered GeoTransolver small-n steel-man
#|   controls (lr 3e-3; 1,000 epochs) land; their falsifier is any control
#|   within 1.2x of MT2 at 35 cases. Data:
#|   results/hilift_ladder_reduction_2026-09-03.json.
#| code-fold: true
import json, statistics
from pathlib import Path
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import matplotlib as mpl
# book palette (mirrors figures.py without importing it: that module
# switches matplotlib to Agg, which suppresses inline output here)
BLUE, RED = "#2a78d6", "#e34948"
INK, INK2, MUTED, GRID, BASELINE = "#0b0b0b", "#52514e", "#898781", "#e1e0d9", "#c3c2b7"
mpl.rcParams.update({"figure.dpi": 110, "font.size": 10, "axes.edgecolor": BASELINE,
                     "axes.labelcolor": INK2, "axes.grid": True, "grid.color": GRID,
                     "xtick.color": MUTED, "ytick.color": MUTED, "xtick.labelcolor": INK2,
                     "ytick.labelcolor": INK2, "axes.spines.top": False,
                     "axes.spines.right": False, "legend.frameon": False})

lad = json.load(open(Path("..") / "results" / "hilift_ladder_reduction_2026-09-03.json"))
rungs = [(35, "lad_hl_{a}_super_scarce_seed{s}"), (210, "lad_hl_{a}_scarce_seed{s}"), (1260, "{a}_hl_lr1_seed{s}")]
data = {}
for arch in ("gt", "mt2"):
    xs, means, lo, hi, pts = [], [], [], [], []
    for n, pat in rungs:
        v = [lad[pat.format(a=arch, s=s)]["pressure_l2"] for s in (42, 43) if pat.format(a=arch, s=s) in lad]
        xs.append(n); means.append(statistics.mean(v)); lo.append(min(v)); hi.append(max(v)); pts.append(v)
    data[arch] = (xs, means, lo, hi, pts)

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(7.2, 4.6))
style = {"gt": (RED, "GeoTransolver", "o"), "mt2": (BLUE, "MeshTransformer2", "s")}
for arch in ("gt", "mt2"):
    xs, means, lo, hi, pts = data[arch]
    c, name, mk = style[arch]
    ax.fill_between(xs, lo, hi, color=c, alpha=0.18, lw=0)
    ax.plot(xs, means, color=c, lw=2.2, marker=mk, ms=7, label=name, zorder=3)
    for x, v in zip(xs, pts):
        ax.scatter([x] * len(v), v, color=c, s=14, alpha=0.9, zorder=4)
    lab_i = 0 if arch == "gt" else 1
    ax.annotate(name, (xs[lab_i], means[lab_i]), xytext=(14, 2 if arch == "gt" else -14),
                textcoords="offset points", color=c, fontsize=10.5, fontweight="bold",
                ha="left", va="center",
                bbox=dict(boxstyle="round,pad=0.15", fc="white", ec="none", alpha=0.85))
gt, mt = data["gt"], data["mt2"]
for i, n in enumerate(gt[0]):
    r = gt[1][i] / mt[1][i]  # GeoTransolver error / MT2 error (>1: MT2 more accurate)
    ymid = (gt[1][i] * mt[1][i]) ** 0.5
    if n < 1000:
        ax.annotate("", (n, mt[1][i]), (n, gt[1][i]),
                    arrowprops=dict(arrowstyle="<->", color=INK2, lw=0.9, shrinkA=4, shrinkB=4))
        ax.text(n * 1.08, ymid, f"GT error = {r:.1f}x MT2", color=INK2, fontsize=9, va="center",
                bbox=dict(boxstyle="round,pad=0.15", fc="white", ec="none", alpha=0.85))
    else:
        ax.annotate(f"{r:.2f}x (parity)", (n, ymid), xytext=(14, 30),
                    textcoords="offset points", color=INK2, fontsize=9, ha="left", va="bottom")
ax.set_xscale("log"); ax.set_yscale("log")
ax.set_xticks([35, 210, 1260]); ax.set_xticklabels(["35\n(super_scarce)", "210\n(scarce)", "1,260\n(full)"])
ax.set_yticks([0.04, 0.06, 0.1, 0.2, 0.4]); ax.set_yticklabels(["0.04", "0.06", "0.10", "0.20", "0.40"])
ax.set_xlim(22, 3200)
ax.set_xlabel("Training cases [count]  (HiLiftAeroML curated splits)", color=INK2)
ax.set_ylabel("Pressure error\nrel-L2 [–]", color=INK2, rotation=0, ha="right", va="center", labelpad=28)
ax.set_title("Data efficiency on HiLiftAeroML: shared 180-case validation set",
             color=INK, loc="left", fontsize=11, pad=14)
ax.grid(True, which="major", color=GRID); ax.grid(False, which="minor")
ax.text(0.01, -0.30,
        "Both architectures: lr 1e-3 (each one's best on the full split), 500 epochs, bf16, no augmentation, "
        "10k points/case,\n2 seeds (band = min–max, dots = seeds). MT2 = v3c constant-gauge config (predates "
        "the similarity gauge).\nTest split sealed. GeoTransolver small-n steel-man controls (lr 3e-3; 1,000 "
        "epochs) are running; result provisional until they land.",
        transform=ax.transAxes, fontsize=7.6, color=MUTED, va="top")
fig.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```

::: {.callout-note title="How to read this figure"}
It says: *with the same budget of training cases, MT2 gets far more
accuracy out of few cases, and the advantage vanishes once data is
plentiful.* It does not say MT2 is more accurate in general (the full-split
point is parity), it does not yet include the small-n steel-man controls
for GeoTransolver, and it says nothing about out-of-distribution
transfer — the aoa and stall axes of the same ladder are reported
separately when their sealed test evaluation is run.
:::

## The frozen instrument {#sec-review-instrument}

Every comparison in this chapter runs on one instrument, frozen on
2026-08-04 and never widened retroactively: DrivAerML surface pressure at
10,000-cell sampling (in-family), a five-resolution sweep (2.5k--40k cells),
zero-shot evaluation on two held-out SHIFT-SUV vehicle families (estate and
fastback, normalized pressure $L_2$ from the fleet-comparable
`metrics.jsonl` pathway), and — added mid-campaign as adversarial probes —
a full random-yaw rotation orbit (P1), a drive-amplitude scaling ladder
(P2), a 10:1 spatially-biased sampling density with exact
Horvitz--Thompson weights (P3), and a shared-prefix companion-set stability
test (P4). Training protocol is identical for every arm ever compared: 500
epochs, batch 1, lr $3\times10^{-3}$ StepLR, bfloat16, no augmentation
unless the augmentation *is* the arm, four-GPU single-node DDP on identical
hardware. A two-point learning-rate parity check ran for both architectures;
it moves the headline gap from 1.18$\times$ to 1.10$\times$ in MT2's favor,
and the symmetric three-point grid of the instrument wave (R1,
@sec-nb-instrument-wave-verdict) fixes the best-vs-best figure at
1.085$\times$ (MT2 at lr $10^{-3}$, 0.0577; GeoTransolver at
$3\times10^{-3}$, 0.0532). Two caveats the critic review made explicit:
every 2026-08/09 verdict rests on two seeds per cell with no paired
statistic, and the instrument is one 48-case validation split of one
dataset.

## The frontier, in one table {#sec-review-frontier}

```{python}
#| label: tbl-frontier
#| output: asis
#| code-fold: true
import json
from pathlib import Path

R = Path("..") / "results" / "mixedres_training_2026-07-31" / "sweep"
mega = json.load(open(R / "mega_reduction.json"))
round3 = json.load(open(R / "round3_reduction.json"))
v3c = json.load(open(R / "mt2_v3c_reduction.json"))

def mean(vals):
    return sum(vals) / len(vals)

gt10 = mean([round3[f"gt_fixed_seed{s}"]["sweep_metrics"]["10000"]["mean"]
             for s in (42, 43, 44)])
gt_zs = mean([round3[f"gt_fixed_seed{s}"]["smoke_estate"]["mean"]
              for s in (42, 43, 44)])

rot_in = mean([mega[f"gt_rotaug_seed{s}"]["in10k"]["mean"] for s in (42, 43)])
rot_zs = mean([mega[f"gt_rotaug_seed{s}"]["estate"]["mean"] for s in (42, 43)])

v3c_in = mean(
    [v3c[f"mt2_v3c_seed{s}"]["sweep"]["10000"]["mean"] for s in (42, 43, 44)]
    + [mega[f"mt2_v3c_seed{s}"]["in10k"]["mean"] for s in (45, 46)]
)
v3c_zs = mean([v3c[f"mt2_v3c_seed{s}"]["smoke_estate"]["mean"] for s in (42, 43, 44)])

mt2m_in = mean([mega[f"mt2_multi_seed{s}"]["in10k"]["mean"] for s in (42, 43, 44)])
mt2m_zs = mean([mega[f"mt2_multi_seed{s}"]["fastback"]["mean"] for s in (42, 43, 44)])
gtm_in = mean([mega[f"gt_multi_seed{s}"]["in10k"]["mean"] for s in (42, 43, 44)])
gtm_zs = mean([mega[f"gt_multi_seed{s}"]["fastback"]["mean"] for s in (42, 43, 44)])

rows = [
    ("GeoTransolver 9M", 1.0, gt_zs, "3.6x", "26-32x broken", "4.6 GB",
     "GeoTransolver reference"),
    ("GT + rotation aug.", rot_in / gt10, rot_zs, "--", "closed (1.00)",
     "4.6 GB", "the augmentation price"),
    ("MT2-v3c (8.6M)", v3c_in / gt10, v3c_zs, "13-14.5x (1.20x with gauge)",
     "exact (1.00)", "9.8 GB", "canonical single-family MT2"),
    ("GT multi-family", gtm_in / gt10, gtm_zs, "--", "26-32x broken",
     "4.6 GB", "zero-shot on HELD-OUT family"),
    ("MT2 multi-family", mt2m_in / gt10, mt2m_zs, "--", "exact (1.00)",
     "9.8 GB", "zero-shot on HELD-OUT family"),
]
out = ("| configuration | in-family (xGT) | zero-shot | density (P3) "
       "| rotation (P1) | peak VRAM | note |\n|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|\n")
for (n, i, z, d, r_, m, note) in rows:
    out += f"| {n} | {i:.2f}x | {z:.2f} | {d} | {r_} | {m} | {note} |\n"
print(out)
print(f": The frontier on the frozen instrument. In-family is normalized "
      f"pressure $L_2$ at 10k cells relative to the GeoTransolver reference "
      f"({gt10:.4f}); zero-shot is the mean normalized pressure $L_2$ on a "
      f"held-out vehicle family (estate for single-family rows, fastback "
      f"for the multi-family rows; 1.0 is mean-predictor level). Peak VRAM "
      f"is training memory at 10,000 tokens on the same four-GPU protocol "
      f"(MT2-v3c 9.81 GB measured in the V6 arm, "
      f"@sec-nb-instrument-wave-verdict; the 5.9 GB this table once "
      f"carried was wrong). The P3 column for MT2 gives the constant-gauge "
      f"v3c figure and, in parentheses, the same model with "
      f"`similarity_gauge` on (@sec-nb-s1-verdict). Sources: "
      f"mega_reduction.json, round3_reduction.json, mt2_v3c_reduction.json.")
```

Three facts to read off the table before any narrative. First, **pose
robustness is a contract, not an accuracy edge.** Closing GeoTransolver's
rotation hole with data augmentation costs it 1.8--1.9$\times$ in-family
(the second row), and this chapter once concluded from that number that
exact equivariance was "worth 1.6$\times$". That comparison used the wrong
steel-man. Canonicalizing GeoTransolver's input frame — freestream to $+x$,
roll fixed from the geometry's principal axes — and training it in that
frame makes it *exactly* pose-invariant at a 1.01$\times$ accuracy cost
(P1'', @sec-nb-p1pp-verdict). What MT2's exact equivariance still buys is
generality: it needs neither a known freestream direction nor a
sign-resolvable principal frame, both of which every vehicle dataset here
happens to supply. Second, **the multi-family rows are a coverage result,
not generalization** (reframed 2026-08-20, @sec-nb-generalization-northstar):
one additional training family moves held-out-family error from
mean-predictor level to 0.11--0.13 for *both* architectures — a
$\sim$7$\times$ improvement that dwarfs every architectural intervention
measured on that axis. This shows that *neither* architecture was
extrapolating beyond its training hull. Measuring generalization — as
scaling curves and beyond-distribution tests rather than points inside an
expanded hull — is the program's current campaign. Third, **the remaining
DrivAerML accuracy gap is small and tuning-sensitive, and it does not
transfer**: 1.18$\times$ at the frozen learning rate, 1.085$\times$ at
best-vs-best rates on DrivAerML (R1), and 0.98 — parity, MT2 nominally
ahead — on HiLiftAeroML at each architecture's best rate
(@sec-nb-hl-verdict). Memory is the cost MT2 pays: 9.8 GB against
GeoTransolver's 4.6 GB at 10,000 tokens; the V6 control shows that
dropping MT2-v3c to 6,500 training tokens brings it to 6.56 GB at an 8%
accuracy cost (@sec-nb-instrument-wave-verdict).

## How we got here: the campaign in five verdicts {#sec-review-arc}

**1. The original MeshTransformer's defects were real, and three closed at root
cause** (@sec-nb-model-quality-agenda ff.). Resolution collapse was a
quadrature-bookkeeping error, cured by measure-consistent
Horvitz--Thompson weighting (@sec-nb-mixedres-verdict). Foreign-family
detonation was the nonlinear read-in's implicit drive degree, removed
exactly by declaring degree one (@sec-nb-bounded-stage1-verdict). Seed
instability collapsed from 2491$\times$ to order-1.3$\times$ as a
byproduct. These closures are the program's clearest demonstrations that
mechanism-first debugging beats remedy-first patching.

**2. GeoTransolver comparison was re-anchored with matched controls, and GeoTransolver
won the measured axes** (@sec-nb-incumbent-stage0-verdict,
@sec-nb-defect4-synthesis). At every resource budget tested,
GeoTransolver dominated in-family accuracy, zero-shot transfer, density
robustness, and training cost — including a resource re-framing
(@sec-nb-resource-accounting) that showed the original matched-*parameter*
comparison had flattered our side. The synthesis recommended inverting the
program: structure the winner rather than accelerate the loser.

**3. The probes made the benchmark's blind spots measurable**
(@sec-nb-contract-probes-synthesis). Rotation: GeoTransolver loses
26--32$\times$ off-pose — every number it posts carries an implicit "in
the dataset's canonical pose" (the P1'/P1'' controls later showed that
the implicit assumption can be made explicit and exact by
canonicalization, @sec-review-reframing). Amplitude: GeoTransolver's
output is drive-amplitude *blind* (layer normalization saturates scale),
while MT2's declared-degree bypass measures exactly 1.0000 — a result
the critic review correctly reduced to a tautology, since the recipe
feeds a unit freestream direction and the bypass multiplies by its norm
(@sec-nb-critic-review). Density: geometry-adaptive statistics pay a
variance-bounded tax; for the kernel-decoder `MeshTransformer` the
measure contract halves the damage (1.7--2.1$\times$ vs GeoTransolver's
3.6$\times$), while for MT2 the same probe read 13--14.5$\times$ until
the S1 gauge repair brought it to 1.20$\times$ (@sec-nb-s1-verdict).

**4. MT2 was built in eleven preregistered iterations, most of which
failed informatively** (@sec-nb-mt2-charter through
@sec-nb-v5-line-verdict). The thesis — GeoTransolver's routing on
exclusively invariant features, contracts paid once at the network edges —
was refuted at v0 (non-separating invariants), remained viable at v0b, shed its
global frames entirely at v2 on Peter's correction that no canonical frame
exists in the physics, and closed its in-family gap by featurization alone
(3.08$\times \to$ 1.15$\times$; capacity was flat at every rung tested).
The accuracy--robustness trade that emerged was then shown to be a
*single-family-training artifact*, dissolved by data diversity rather than
architecture.

**5. Query-independence was priced, and the price is the finding**
(@sec-nb-v5-line-verdict). Three passive-decoder designs either collapsed
in training or, once the collapse was fixed by a local token readout,
converged 2.7$\times$ worse in-family while achieving the best density
robustness of any variant. Conclusion, now measured rather than argued:
**in this design family, accuracy and query-interaction are entangled** —
the query-side token stream is where the accuracy comes from, which is
also precisely why the accurate models carry companion-set sensitivity
(2% for GeoTransolver, 6.8% for MT2-v3c on the P4 probe). A deployable
surrogate can have exact evaluate-anywhere semantics at 3.9$\times$ the
error, or near-GeoTransolver accuracy with single-digit-percent sensitivity;
it cannot currently have both.

## The refutation wave: every open mechanism candidate, resolved {#sec-review-refutation-wave}

The G1/G2 scaling ladder (@sec-nb-g1g2-verdict) gave the mechanism hunt
its target: **the G2 transfer gap** — GeoTransolver's zero-shot error on
a held-out vehicle family improves monotonically with in-family training
data (0.784 → 0.657 across five training-set-size rungs) while
MeshTransformer2's stays flat at 0.83–0.94. Between 2026-08-20 and
2026-08-21, five preregistered lines appeared to resolve every candidate
explanation then on the table. Two of those closures (M1, M4) were later
voided or retracted by the critic review and re-measured by S1
(@sec-review-reframing); each verdict below carries its current status
and is dated and anchored.

**Locality: refuted as the transfer carrier** (@sec-nb-locality-verdict).
The hypothesis that GeoTransolver's transfer compounding is carried by
local features predicted that MeshTransformer2's flag-gated local
patch-integral channel would bend MT2's G2 curve downward. Measured: the
local channel yields a consistent but *constant* 3–5% in-family improvement
(the ratio to plain MT2 rises 0.953 → 0.972 across rungs — an offset,
not a slope change), does not improve zero-shot transfer, and
*destabilizes* it at the largest rung (n=218 seed spread 0.12 vs 0.02
in-family). The channel remains an MT3 candidate only as a cheap in-family
offset.

**The literature wave: all four arms resolved one day after
preregistration** (prereg 69a81e2a, @sec-nb-lit-wave-prereg;
wave-close @sec-nb-m1-verdict-wave-close):

- **M1 scale relaxation: verdict VOID** (@sec-nb-m1-verdict-wave-close,
  voided at @sec-nb-critic-review). The arm appended a log
  raw-cloud-radius scalar to "break MT2's exact scale equivariance" and
  read a null (1.3–2.0% in-family, inside the ±3% seed band). MT2 never
  had scale equivariance: its constant `reference_length` already let
  the backbone see absolute size, so the added feature was redundant by
  construction and the null was guaranteed. The over-symmetrization
  hypothesis was never tested. The S1 gauge arm (@sec-review-reframing)
  is the first experiment to actually vary MT2's scale behaviour.
- **M2 anchor-conditioned decode: CLOSED, twice** (@sec-nb-v5a4-gate,
  then V6 at @sec-nb-instrument-wave-verdict). The AB-UPT-style design
  (a fixed 2,560-token interacting anchor core, all queries decoding
  passively) first failed its accuracy-only pilot gate by 1.2% — a
  closure the campaign review flagged as a judgment error, because the
  arm ran at 65% of v3c's memory and the resource frame was not
  applied (@sec-nb-campaign-review). V6 re-opened it at matched peak
  VRAM (v5a4 6.35 GB vs v3c at 6,500 tokens 6.56 GB): 0.209/0.221
  against the control's 0.0697/0.0671, 3.1$\times$ worse and far past
  the 1.3$\times$ closure bar, with a *slower* validation step on
  DrivAerML. The query-independence price finding of
  @sec-nb-v5-line-verdict stands, now resource-normalized.
- **M3 invariant completeness: PARTIAL, and its by-product closed
  negative** (@sec-nb-m3-verdict; @sec-nb-parity-thread-closed). An
  expressivity ceiling is real — geometries with a discrete rotational
  symmetry about the drive axis are provably invisible to MT2's
  invariant set — but it is refuted as a DrivAerML-scale limitation (no
  car has such a symmetry; 1° of drive misalignment restores
  separation). The audit also found a **reflection-covariance defect in
  MT2's vector head**. Six exactly covariant repairs were then trained
  and every one either cost $\geq 12\%$ wall shear or failed to train;
  the labels are mirror-covariant to $<1\%$ and the default head's
  predictions are empirically covariant, so the default is retained and
  the honest contract is SE(3), not O(3) (@sec-mt2-architecture has the
  ledger).
- **M4 NEO normalization audit: RETRACTED, then REFUTED by S1**
  (@sec-nb-lit-wave-prereg; retracted at @sec-nb-critic-review; refuted
  at @sec-nb-s1-verdict). The audit concluded MT2 was already
  measure-complete and the P3 density floor information-limited. It
  missed the first line of the geometry reduction: the centroid was an
  unweighted mean, shifting 0.94 RMS radii under 10:1 bias. Replacing
  it with the measure-weighted centroid and RMS-radius gauge cut MT2's
  P3 penalty from 13–14.5$\times$ to 1.20$\times$ at no in-family cost.
  The floor was an implementation gap.

**G3, the boundary-condition axis: contracts guarantee only what they
declare — and an exact kernel decoder generalizes across frequency
content where learned routing does not** (@sec-nb-g3-verdict, overturned
in part at @sec-nb-g3-kernel-rerun). On the exact-label 2D
conformal-Laplace suite, the drive-linearity contract makes amplitude
extrapolation *free* — exact at ×2 and ×4 amplitude — while the two
learned-amplitude arms degrade 6–12× (MT2+BC-scalar) and 4.5–7×
(soft-slice): the first measured price of an undeclared linearity. The
original verdict went on to say that *no* arm generalizes across BC
frequency content (rel-L2 ≈ 1.0 on unseen drive modes) and called this
a data-coverage limit. That sentence measured the wrong arm: the
`MeshTransformer` arm used the *moment* query decoder, whose proved
$m \le 2$ angular ceiling (@sec-mesh-attention) makes the T1 test —
drive modes 5–8, pure $m \ge 3$ content — structurally unrepresentable,
so rel-L2 ≈ 1.0 was guaranteed. Rerun with the exact double-layer
kernel decoder (a post-hoc decoder control, labelled as such, three
seeds), `MeshTransformer` scores **T1 0.070** — 14× better than the
moment decoder and reproducing chapter 6's 0.075 under G3's protocol —
and is the best arm on every G3 axis: 4× lower in-distribution error
than the next best, exact amplitude extrapolation, and the lowest
geometry-OOD error. The corrected statement: the soft-slice family
(MT2+BC-scalar, the GeoTransolver-family mechanism) and the moment
decoder fail on the frequency axis; an exact Green's-function operator
carries the PDE's spectral response for free. This is the strongest
generalization result the program owns, and it belongs to the
architecture line the program pivoted away from.

**What remains.** Locality is refuted; the expressivity ceiling is ruled
out at DrivAerML scale; the normalization floor was an implementation
gap, now closed; and the scale axis has finally been tested — S1 made
MT2 genuinely similarity-covariant and its zero-shot estate error did
not move (0.949 vs 0.967, inside the two-seed spread), so absolute size
was not the cross-family leak (@sec-nb-s1-verdict). The earlier
hypothesis that GeoTransolver "learns what exact similarity equivariance
forbids MT2 from learning" cannot be right as stated: MT2 was not
scale-equivariant, and both models saw absolute size in the same units.
The remaining candidate for the G2 transfer gap is GeoTransolver's
**pointwise raw coordinate features** and non-equivariant encoder, with
the HiLift generalization ladder (launched at LR 1e-3 for both
architectures after the high-lift parity verdict, @sec-nb-hl-verdict) as
the discriminator in flight.

## What this does not solve {#sec-review-honesty}

The claims above are scoped by construction, and the scoping is part of
the result. The industrial evidence rests on two automotive dataset
families plus one high-lift aircraft dataset; every industrial run is
surface $\to$ surface, and the boundary $\to$ *interior* problem the
program's statement of scope names has never been run with MT2 (the
volume recipes exist in the tree). Boundary-condition variation is
measured only in 2D with exact labels (the G3 suite); its corrected
verdict — amplitude generalization is purchasable by a declared linearity
contract at a measured 4.5--12$\times$ value, and frequency-content
generalization is purchasable by an exact kernel decoder but by no
soft-slice mechanism tested (@sec-nb-g3-kernel-rerun) — is what any 3D
BC-varying dataset decision should be built on. Whether that kernel
result transfers to 3D aerodynamics was gated on a zero-parameter test
and the gate failed: an exact potential-flow oracle scores rel-L2 4.8 on
DrivAerML pressure against 0.77 for predicting the case mean, because
the dominant physics is separation, which no Laplace operator carries
(K0, @sec-nb-k0-verdict). The "structure buys generalization" thesis is
therefore bounded exactly where the available structure stops matching
the PDE. The typed-BC ingestion that distinguishes the GLOBE lineage
remains unbuilt at industrial scale for the same reason as before: no
*industrial* benchmark can yet measure it. Density robustness is
1.20$\times$ under a 10:1 sampling bias for MT2 with the similarity
gauge and 13--14.5$\times$ for the constant-gauge checkpoints this book
mostly reports (@sec-nb-s1-verdict). Both architectures misbehave at
scale extremes under the frozen learning rate (seed-conditioned
detonations at 11M for the original MeshTransformer; a turned frontier
at 564M for GeoTransolver), so no "scales to very large runs" claim is
made by either side. Finally, the DrivAerML gap is *not* explained. The
high-lift wave showed it does not transfer (parity at 0.98,
@sec-nb-hl-verdict), and the campaign review read that as evidence the
gap was DrivAerML's time-averaged label noise — but the N1 probe built
to test that attribution did not discriminate: the four-model
shared-residual fraction is 0.71 on DrivAerML and 0.70 on the
cleaner-label HiLift control (@sec-nb-n1-verdict). The honest statement
is narrower: the gap does not transfer across datasets, and the
residuals on both are dominated by structure common to both
architectures, which this probe cannot split into label noise and shared
inductive bias.

## Roads from here {#sec-review-roads}

In recommended order: (1) a scoped experimental release of MT2 with the
similarity gauge as its reference configuration — "SE(3)-equivariant
surface aero surrogate at GeoTransolver-class accuracy, learning-rate
robust and density robust, at about twice the training memory" — with the
R1 and S1 measurements as its headline evidence and the entanglement
finding as its stated limitation; (2) the HiLift generalization ladder
(running, launched after the parity verdict of @sec-nb-hl-verdict) — the
Reynolds-varying analogue of the G1/G2 ladder and the last discriminator
in flight for the G2-gap candidates — which gates the MT3 preregistration
(@sec-tech-tree); (3) the volume-target run the program's scope statement
demands, on `drivaer_ml_volume` or `highlift_volume`, which also decides
whether MT2's query-side dependence forces the passive decoder's measured
3$\times$ price at $10^5$--$10^6$ interior queries; (4) the upstream PR
series for the engineering bycatch (rank-failure barrier,
distributed-timeout knob, degenerate-cell guards, measure infrastructure —
all verified still absent upstream); (5) any 3D BC-varying dataset
decision, now informed by the corrected 2D G3 fingerprint
(@sec-nb-g3-kernel-rerun): build it for amplitude, geometry, *and*
frequency content, because an exact kernel decoder does generalize on the
last axis — while remembering that K0 (@sec-nb-k0-verdict) bounds the
exact-kernel line to problems whose operator the kernel actually is; and
(6) the closed query-independence line — the fully passive decode priced
at 2.7$\times$ (@sec-nb-v5-line-verdict) and the anchor-conditioned
variant closed at matched VRAM at 3.1$\times$
(@sec-nb-instrument-wave-verdict) — revisited only if a deployment
actually demands evaluate-anywhere semantics at the measured price, and
then against AB-UPT as a measured baseline rather than against MT2
itself.

## The 2026-09 reframing: what the instrument wave and the critic review changed {#sec-review-reframing}

Between 2026-09-01 and 2026-09-03 the program ran an instrument wave
(@sec-nb-campaign-review), commissioned an independent critic review of
the entire written record (@sec-nb-critic-review;
`results/critic_review_2026-09-02.md`, seventeen graded claims), and ran
the controls that review asked for. Several sentences the earlier
sections of this chapter and @sec-mt2-architecture carried were
contradicted by the program's own code or artifacts. This section is the
ledger of what was retired and what replaced it; the notebook entries
hold the numbers.

**Retired: "MT2 is similarity-equivariant" and "MT2 is
measure-complete."** MT2 in its original form is SE(3)-equivariant only.
Its reference length was a constant, so a 2$\times$ geometric rescale
changed the output by 63%, and its centroid was an unweighted mean that
shifted 0.94 RMS radii under 10:1 biased sampling (both verified against
the code, @sec-nb-critic-review). The M1 verdict is void and the M4
closure was retracted. The repair — the `similarity_gauge` flag,
measure-weighted centroid and RMS-radius gauge, with a geometric-scale
contract test — is free in-family and cuts the P3 density penalty from
13--14.5$\times$ to 1.20$\times$ (S1, @sec-nb-s1-verdict). It is the
reference configuration for new runs; frozen checkpoints keep the
constant gauge.

**Retired: "exact equivariance is worth 1.6$\times$."** The
augmentation baseline was the wrong steel-man. Canonicalizing
GeoTransolver's input frame at evaluation time already made a frozen
checkpoint exactly pose-invariant, at a 1.6--1.7$\times$ in-pose penalty
traced to hypersensitivity to sub-degree frame tilt (1° of roll costs
1.7--1.8$\times$; P1', @sec-nb-p1-canon-verdict). Training GeoTransolver
in the canonical frame removed even that: exact pose invariance at
1.01$\times$ cost (P1'', @sec-nb-p1pp-verdict). MT2's exact equivariance
remains a genuine *contract* — it needs no known freestream direction
and no sign-resolvable principal frame, whereas canonicalization needs
both — but on the vehicle datasets this program measures (0/48 degenerate
frames; skewness sign consistent 48/48) it is not an accuracy advantage.

**Retired: "equal-or-lower cost."** MT2-v3c peaks at 9.8 GB of training
memory at 10,000 tokens on the same DrivAerML protocol where
GeoTransolver peaks at 4.6 GB (V6, @sec-nb-instrument-wave-verdict); the
frontier table's earlier 5.9 GB was wrong. At 6,500 tokens MT2 runs in
6.56 GB at an 8% accuracy cost.

**Retired: "the DrivAerML gap was label noise."** The N1 shared-residual
probe does not discriminate (0.71 on DrivAerML vs 0.70 on the HiLift
control, @sec-nb-n1-verdict). The high-lift parity measurement stands;
its explanation does not.

**Retired: "no architecture generalizes across BC frequency content."**
The G3 `MeshTransformer` arm used the moment decoder with the proved
$m \le 2$ nullspace, so the T1 test was unrepresentable by construction.
The kernel-decoder rerun scores T1 0.070 and wins every G3 axis
(@sec-nb-g3-kernel-rerun). Whether this transfers to 3D aerodynamics was
then gated on the K0 potential-flow oracle, which failed by a factor of
five (rel-L2 4.8 vs 0.77 for the case mean, @sec-nb-k0-verdict): for a
bluff separated body there is no cheap exact operator, so the K1/K2
learned-kernel arms did not launch.

**Retired: the drive-degree contract as a merit.** Inert on
unit-direction inputs and the wrong law for pressure in any case
(@sec-mt2-architecture).

**Closed negative: exact reflection covariance of the vector head.** Six
constructions, all $\geq 12\%$ worse on wall shear or untrainable;
labels covariant to $<1\%$; default retained
(@sec-nb-parity-thread-closed).

**Confirmed: learning-rate robustness is an architecture property (R1,
@sec-nb-instrument-wave-verdict).** On the symmetric DrivAerML grid
$\{10^{-3}, 3\times10^{-3}, 10^{-2}\}$, GeoTransolver degrades
4--14$\times$ at $10^{-2}$ (0.739/0.221 against its best 0.0532) while
MT2 degrades 1.55$\times$ (0.0874/0.0914 against 0.0577); the same
pattern held on HiLift (MT2 0.040--0.049 across the whole grid,
GeoTransolver 0.041--0.397). One caveat from N1: MT2 has the *larger*
seed-to-seed prediction spread on both datasets, so robustness to
learning rate and robustness to seed are different properties.

**The honest MT2 claim set, after this week.** (i) Exact SE(3)
equivariance as a contract — no frame needed, valid for degenerate
geometries and unknown freestreams — but not an accuracy edge on
vehicle data. (ii) Learning-rate robustness: 1.55$\times$ degradation
across a decade where GeoTransolver loses 4--14$\times$. (iii)
Biased-density robustness of 1.20$\times$ with the similarity gauge,
against GeoTransolver's 3.6$\times$. (iv) In-family parity with
GeoTransolver on HiLiftAeroML at best learning rate (MT2/GT = 0.98) and a
1.085$\times$ deficit on DrivAerML at best-vs-best rates. (v) About
twice GeoTransolver's peak training memory. Every one of these is a
two-seed measurement on one validation split per dataset; none has a
paired statistic behind it yet.
